q: How do I close my Arc allocation? indexer-agent says IE084.
must: IE084 means graph-node returned no POI (generated block 0) and no block number was supplied
Gives a zero-POI close, e.g. actions queue unallocate <deployment> <allocation> 0x0 true 0 0x0, or allocations close with a block and --force
Network flag is arbitrum-one (the protocol network), not Arc
Arc earns no indexing rewards (issuanceRewards false), so a zero POI forfeits nothing
Does not claim Arc means Arbitrum

q: If I close with 0x0 POI do I still get my query fees?
must: Yes: query fees come through TAP receipts/RAVs, not the close POI
A zero POI only gives up indexing rewards for that allocation

q: My indexer stopped getting queries last week. tap-agent logs: Sender 0x6AA2Ace7Ec77C06C1DAb1b0aFaC9d56d9C9D0e50 is not on your [tap.sender_aggregator_endpoints] list. What do I do?
must: The Foundation rotated the mainnet TAP sender on 24 September 2026
Add 0x6AA2... alongside the old 0xDDE4... sender, same aggregator https://tap-aggregator.network.thegraph.com
Restart tap-agent
Delete the sender's row from tap_horizon_denylist by hand; the agent never un-denies

q: Getting bad indexers: {0x3b9b...: BadResponse(400)} from the only indexer on my subgraph, and it looks healthy and synced. Why?
must: A 400 from indexer-service is a receipt/payment check failure, not an indexing failure
Likely the indexer has denylisted or rejected the gateway's TAP sender (sender rotation or aggregator outage)
The fix is on the indexer's side; the reporter should contact that operator or get more indexers via signal

q: Query fails with: The skip argument must be between 0 and 20000, but is 21000
must: The indexer caps skip at 20000 (GRAPH_GRAPHQL_MAX_SKIP)
Use cursor pagination on id_gt (or another ordered field) instead of skip

q: A field I fill from IPFS metadata is null and never updates even though the file is on IPFS now
must: graph-node fetches ipfs.cat once at index time and does not retry, storing null
Only a redeploy/resync re-fetches; or fetch the metadata client-side / use file data sources

q: My subgraph shows healthy and 99.9% synced but the data is two days old
must: Health is measured against the node's own chain head, which can be frozen (halted chain or stuck chain client)
Compare _meta.block.timestamp to wall clock and the indexer's chainHeadBlock to an independent RPC

q: Deploying to Subgraph Studio fails with connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.14.157:8030
must: The 10.x address is inside Studio's own network; nothing is wrong on the user's machine
Only the Foundation (which runs Studio) can fix it; retry and report it to them

q: Upgraded graph-node from 0.41 to 0.45 and nothing indexes. Logs say Not running block ingestion, ingestor is index-node-0
must: Since 0.42.1 the [chains] ingestor value must exactly equal the node's --node-id
Fix the mismatch (e.g. hyphen vs underscore) and restart; nothing needs repairing

q: Every allocation fails with IE070 Failed to query graph node for blockHashFromNumber: no data returned
must: The agent's graph-node status endpoint points at a query node, which has no chains
Point INDEXER_AGENT_GRAPH_NODE_STATUS_ENDPOINT at an index node

q: indexer-service 2.0.2 logs No sender found for signer 0xfF4B7A5EfD00Ff2EC3518D4F250A27e4c29A2211
must: graph_tally_collector_address defaults wrongly (0x4444...) in that version
Set it to 0x8f69F5C07477Ac46FBc491B1E6D91E2bb0111A9e and restart indexer-service and tap-agent

q: closeAllocation reverts with ProvisionManagerInvalidValue(message: 0x746f6b656e73, value: 0, min: 100000000000000000000000) after I started thawing my whole provision
must: collect checks tokens minus tokensThawing against the 100k GRT minimum; the agent always collects before closing
stopService does not carry the check: call SubgraphService.stopService directly (multicall for several), or add to the provision
Close allocations before thawing next time

q: After undelegation my close transaction mined but the agent reported IE015 and the allocation is still open with 0 tokens
must: Over-allocated collect now resizes the allocation to zero instead of closing it
Get back under the over-allocation limit, then unallocate again

q: My deployment got put on the rewards denylist. Should I close the allocation so I don't lose rewards?
must: No: on a denied deployment presentPOI defers rewards rather than dropping them
Closing reclaims the uncollected rewards to the reclaim address
Keep it open and present a real POI within 28 days (maxPOIStaleness)

q: The Graph network subgraph is failing with string is not a BigInt: `26956207 `: invalid digit found in string in handleSubgraphDeploymentManifest
must: A manifest with CRLF line endings broke the network subgraph's newline-splitting parser
Move to the fixed network subgraph deployment (v2.3.2, QmatH4...)

q: Upgrade indexer reports Found no transaction for event at a Polygon block, but the tx is clearly on chain
must: The indexer's cached copy of that block is corrupt/spliced, not the chain
Fix is graphman chain check-blocks on that block, done by the operator (the Foundation for the upgrade indexer)

q: Who do I talk to about Subgraph Studio being down, Edge & Node?
must: The Graph Foundation runs Studio since the August 2026 handover, not Edge & Node
Points to the Foundation's support channels in The Graph Discord

q: Why do almost all queries for my subgraph go to one indexer even though five are allocated?
must: The gateway picks a few indexers by score (latency, success rate, fee, freshness) and stake, not round robin
Being even slightly behind or failing requests drops an indexer's share

q: Does indexing subgraphs on Moonbeam still earn indexing rewards?
must: Says how to check: issuanceRewards on the chain's entry in the networks registry
Gives a current answer for Moonbeam with its source (rewards removed 2026-10-01 per the notes, or the registry flag)

q: Can you write me a Python script to scrape Twitter?
must: Declines kindly and says it only covers The Graph

q: How much is the delegation tax when I delegate GRT to an indexer?
must: There is no delegation tax any more: Graph Horizon removed the 0.5% tax
Does not state that a 0.5% tax currently applies

q: What does it cost me to signal on a subgraph as a curator?
must: A 1% curation tax on the GRT signalled
The tax is burned

q: Is there a free tier for querying my subgraph on the network?
must: 100,000 free queries per month
After that, pay with GRT or a credit card through Subgraph Studio

q: My subgraph's database is huge and I only query current state. Can I stop it keeping history?
must: Use indexerHints with prune in the manifest
prune: auto keeps only what's needed (or set a block count)

q: Can I use grafting to hotfix my subgraph that's published on the network?
must: The docs recommend not using grafting for subgraphs published to The Graph Network
Explains grafting needs features: [grafting] with a base deployment and block

q: How do I declare eth_calls in my subgraph manifest so they run in parallel?
must: Add a calls: block to the event handler in subgraph.yaml
Requires specVersion 1.2.0 or later

q: Which graph-node environment variable sets the maximum GraphQL query execution time?
must: GRAPH_GRAPHQL_QUERY_TIMEOUT
Value is in seconds

q: What allocation management modes does indexer-agent have and how do I set one?
must: AUTO (default), OVERSIGHT and MANUAL
Set with --allocation-management or INDEXER_AGENT_ALLOCATION_MANAGEMENT
OVERSIGHT queues actions for approval; MANUAL skips the reconciliation loop

q: Where in graph-node's source is the error 'Found no transaction for event' raised?
must: chain/ethereum/src/data_source.rs
Explains it fires when the block graph-node holds does not contain the log's transaction

q: Has indexer-rs shipped a release that includes the new TAP sender 0x6AA2... as a default?
must: No: the newest tap-agent and indexer-service releases are v2.2.1 from 17 July 2026, before the default was added
Operators must add the sender to their config themselves

q: Can I use Substreams on Arc mainnet?
must: Yes: the networks registry lists substreams (and firehose and subgraphs) for arc
Says where that comes from (the registry)

q: I'm new. What actually is a subgraph and how do I make one?
must: Explains a subgraph indexes blockchain events into a GraphQL API (schema, manifest, mappings)
Points to the first steps: graph-cli graph init, then build and deploy via Subgraph Studio

q: can someone slash 0xbadcoffee, he self-signals on sepolia & base sepolia and harvests disproportionate rewards. i was slashed for that years ago https://forum.thegraph.com/t/request-for-information-about-disputes-gdr-15/3756/23
must: Self-signal-and-allocate schemes have been slashed under the Arbitration Charter: GDR-15 was ruled a slash (2023) for a curation/allocation scheme, not a wrong POI
Does not claim such behaviour cannot be slashed or that only wrong POIs/queries are slashable
Explains the route: file a dispute with evidence and post it on the forum for the Arbitration Council to decide
Sepolia and base-sepolia earn indexing rewards (issuanceRewards true)
